Appreciate the context and the report. We ran the numbers with product/ops and put together three options that balance unit economics and operational predictability. Short summary here and a link to the proposal doc below.

Options (monthly committed tokens; burst pocket; expected effective rate):

1) Conservative steady (no big change) — 10M tokens/month; 20% burst pocket; current rates
2) Growth commit (recommended) — 14M tokens/month (+40%); 35% burst pocket; 12% volume discount on hosted API unit rate
3) Aggressive reserved (best price) — 20M tokens/month (+100%); 50% burst pocket; 22% discount, requires 12-month commit and a 30% prepayment

Key notes:
- We can configure a burst pocket that caps burst spend per billing period and triggers alerts at 75/90%.
- p95 latency SLO: we can include a 450ms target in the SLA for the Growth commit on our Dedicated routing policy for retail workloads.
- Invoicing: monthly or annual invoicing available; procurement usually prefers annual with PO and net-30.

Link to proposal: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-retailnova-proposal 

Next steps I suggest:
- Internal alignment on option 2 (Growth commit)
- Draft SOW & payment terms for procurement to review (we can send a redline-ready SOW)
- Target sign by Aug 20 to cover Q4 planning

Looping in Priyom for pricing confirmation and Laura for onboarding/ops checklist.

Thanks for the quick turn. Attached is the redline-ready SOW (RN_DN-4521_SOW_draft.docx) and a short one-page summary of the pricing bands. Summary: we recommend Option 2 (Growth commit) — 14M tokens/month, 35% burst pocket, 12% unit discount for a 12-month rolling commitment. If RetailNova elects annual prepay (30% upfront) we can move to Option 3 pricing (22% discount) and expand burst to 50%.
